subject: POC Readiness & MAP — Veridian Labs: org seed, API keys, allowlist, VPC peering
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@veridianlabs.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@veridianlabs.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Veridian POC — next steps & gating list

Vivek / team,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the Veridian engineering and product leads were impressed. We'd like to move forward with a 4-week POC focused on inference latency and cost for our clinical summarization pipeline. Before we lock dates, can you send a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that clearly lists the environment gating items we need to complete on our side and yours? High-priority items from our side: 

- Org/tenant setup (seed account for Veridian, SSO options)
- API key model (ephemeral vs long-lived service keys) and token rotation cadence
- IP allowlist details and expected CIDR ranges to add to our firewall
- VPC peering model and target maintenance window (we prefer low-traffic nights)
- Data residency and retention defaults for the POC

Target timeline: 4 weeks from kickoff, with a technical handoff + peering window in week 1. We also need a basic SOC 2 attestation + evidence list so our security team can sign off.

If you can share the MAP + a one-page checklist and a sample peering template, we can route internally tomorrow. Attaching our procurement summary for context (procurement-summary.pdf).

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of AI, Veridian Labs
Attachments: procurement-summary.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@veridianlabs.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Veridian POC — next steps & gating list

Samir — great to hear, and thanks for the clear list. I've sketched a compact MAP (attached) and a proposed 4-week close cadence so your team has visibility. High-level plan (summary):

1) Week 0 (pre-kick): org seed + SSO, procurement paperwork, SOC2 request submitted
2) Week 1 (kick + networking): create project tenant, generate initial service account + one ephemeral API key for smoke tests, VPC peering slot, IP allowlist applied
3) Week 2 (integration): full traffic simulation, batching/kv cache tuning, metrics collection hooks
4) Week 3 (optimization): quantization/batching experiments, cost/reporting dashboard setup
5) Week 4 (acceptance): final runbook, handoff notes, evaluation snapshot and recommendations

Key ask for Veridian (what we'd like you to provide):
- Preferred peering window (dates/times) and the firewall ticket owner
- Public egress IP block(s) to allow (we'll confirm our side ranges)
- SSO metadata if you prefer IdP-first org seed

Attachments I put in the Drive and attached here: Veridian_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP + owners), vpc-peering-template.yaml (peer config example). Link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1VeridianMAP

Jonas and Neha will be on the technical working session. Suggested next step: 60-minute tech call Wednesday 11/11 at 10:30 PT to walk the peering template and firewall checklist. If that works, we'll reserve the slot and send calendar invites.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Platform Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Veridian_MAP_v1.xlsx, vpc-peering-template.yaml

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@veridianlabs.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Veridian POC — next steps & gating list

Samir / Vivek — quick technical notes to make the peering & API-key flow straightforward. Copying the relevant items from the MAP for visibility.

Network: 
- Redwood side egress: 34.198.120.0/22 and 52.23.64.0/20 (we'll provide a formal allowlist file)
- For peering we prefer asymmetric route acceptance: create a VPC-to-VPC peer using the template and allow peer ASN 64512
- Proposed maintenance window: Wed 2026-11-17 01:00–03:00 PT (low traffic). If that conflicts, give two alternative windows.

Auth & keys: 
- We'll seed your org with a service account. Recommended pattern: one long-lived admin key for onboarding (rotate at day 7), and ephemeral session keys for tests (TTL 12 hours) issued via a short-lived token exchange.
- Ephemeral keys support automatic KV cache mapping for session affinity; TTL default 12h but can be reduced to 4h for higher security.

Preflight checklist (what I need from Veridian before peering):
- Firewall ticket number + point of contact
- VPC CIDR for peer connection and example route table entry
- Any egress proxy rules that might rewrite TLS SNI (we need direct TLS)

I've attached a plain text allowlist you can hand to networking (network-allowlist.txt) and the peering template already referenced. We'll run a dry-run in a sandbox before the scheduled window.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: network-allowlist.txt

On Tue, Nov 10, 2026 at 11:04 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Samir — great to hear, and thanks for the clear list...

From: Samir Patel <samir@veridianlabs.com>

Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@veridianlabs.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Veridian POC — next steps & gating list

Thanks Vivek / Jonas — this looks good.

Confirming: Wednesday 2026-11-17 01:00–03:00 PT works for our infra team. I'll open a firewall change ticket (CHG-74291) and share the ticket owner by EOD tomorrow. We'll also attach the SOC 2 evidence request (SOC2-request.pdf) to the same thread for your security team.

Next steps for us:
- Laura will send SSO metadata if we go that route (expect by EOD)
- I will share our VPC CIDR and the firewall ticket by EOD tomorrow

Appreciate the clear MAP — the Veridian exec sponsor is aligned on the 4-week cadence. Looking forward to the tech call on 11/11 at 10:30 PT.

Samir
Head of AI, Veridian Labs
Attachments referenced: SOC2-request.pdf
